source.title: Data-Dependent Stability of Stochastic Gradient Descent

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no material text problem noted.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses a different, data-dependent stability bound and reports an empirical comparison with an estimated generalization error. It does not test the specific interventions or measurements named in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper reports an empirical comparison of its non-convex data-dependent bound, the uniform bound, and an empirical generalization-error estimate. Results cited from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves SGD stability bounds and compares their estimated tightness on an MNIST CNN. None of its own results tests V1–V8. Its initialization-curvature analysis does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare its ranking of generalization gaps with other measures, as V7 requires.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors prove data-dependent stability bounds for convex and non-convex smooth losses; initialization risk and, in the non-convex case, expected initialization curvature enter these bounds. Their MNIST experiment reports tighter estimated bounds than the uniform counterpart. They also derive optimistic rates under vanishing empirical risk and propose initialization selection for transfer learning, leaving its experimental evaluation to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops distribution-dependent algorithmic stability bounds for SGD; the empirical comparison estimates bound tightness rather than testing a claim-version intervention or measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The empirical bound depends on the initialization point; multiple pre-trained warm-starts are reported to yield tighter estimates.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.2.1 reports an estimated data-dependent stability bound roughly one order of magnitude tighter than the uniform bound on an MNIST CNN. Warm-start calculations suggest further tightening, potentially because validation loss supplies a decreasing estimate of initialization risk.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-dependent SGD stability bounds can provide tighter estimated generalization guarantees than uniform stability bounds in an MNIST CNN experiment.

record.problems: The empirical evidence is one MNIST CNN experiment; constants are estimated, and the plotted bound values are not given numerically in the text. The authors describe the warm-start comparison as suggestive.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results identified. Theoretical bounds and transfer-learning proposals are not separate empirical outcomes on the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with observed generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Curvature enters a theoretical upper bound here; this is not an empirical test of V7's magnitude-aware sharpness correlation. References to random-label memorization and large-batch sharp minima are prior-work discussion.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as network width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Effect of removing memorized examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: convolutional neural network with three convolutional layers interlaced with max-pooling, followed by the fully connected layer with 16 units
rows.operation_detail: Compared the data-dependent generalization bound with the uniform bound and an empirical estimate of generalization error.

conditions.value: multiple warm-starts; 7 such warm-starts at every 200 steps

rows.measure: Tightness of generalization bounds against the empirical estimate, defined as the absolute difference of validation and training average losses.
rows.value: data-dependent bound (1); tighter estimate by roughly one order of magnitude
rows.note: Authors state that pre-trained warm-starts suggest even tighter estimates; the plotted values are not reproduced numerically in the supplied text.
rows.check: This is a comparison of the authors' bound with a prior bound, not an outcome on any claim version. Retain only under fits_no_version. The reported order-of-magnitude improvement concerns estimated bounds using empirically estimated constants; it does not establish a corresponding reduction in actual generalization error. The architecture, dataset and warm-start description match Section 5.2.1.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
